security_audit.summary: All 36 static detections are false positives caused by Markdown syntax, relative documentation links, contract-template language, and homepage metadata. The reviewed files contain no executable shell commands, network requests, path-traversal operation, or prompt-injection attempt. The skill does describe local draft storage and optional connectors, so users should control any host permissions.

remediation.issue: Relative links and Markdown backticks trigger high-volume static alerts.
remediation.suggestion: Tune the scanner to distinguish Markdown links and code formatting from executable filesystem and shell operations.

remediation.issue: The skill describes saving drafts and submitting an authorized registry proposal.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before writing persistent records or invoking any optional connector.

remediation.issue: Agreement templates provide general guidance only.
remediation.suggestion: Keep the legal-review warning prominent and ask for jurisdiction-specific review before execution.

content.value_statement: Influencer agreements often leave payment, usage rights, and approval terms unclear. This skill structures a draft or review checklist so teams can identify terms that need negotiation or legal review.
actual_capabilities: Gathers parties, deliverables, compensation, platforms, and requested contract terms.
Drafts an influencer agreement framework with eleven core contract sections.
Explains the purpose and negotiation concerns for material agreement clauses.
Reviews pasted contract terms against an essential-terms and red-flags checklist.
Creates negotiation guidance for usage rights, exclusivity, revisions, approval, and payment.
limitations: Provides general information and templates, not legal advice.
Does not determine whether terms comply with a specific jurisdiction.
Requires accurate deal details and pasted terms from the user.
Cannot sign contracts or send them through an e-signature service by itself.

use_cases.title: Create a campaign agreement
use_cases.description: Turn an agreed creator campaign scope into a structured draft with deliverables, payment, rights, and disclosure terms.

use_cases.title: Review agency paper
use_cases.description: Check a pasted agency agreement for missing terms, broad rights, and negotiation issues before counsel reviews it.

use_cases.title: Build a reusable template
use_cases.description: Create a repeatable partnership agreement structure for common campaign types and approval workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a simple agreement
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a simple influencer agreement for two Instagram posts. The fee is $500. Include a payment schedule, 12-month non-exclusive owned-channel usage, and disclosure requirements.

prompt_templates.title: Review pasted terms
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these creator agreement terms. List missing essential terms, red flags, and questions for legal counsel: [paste terms].

prompt_templates.title: Compare usage-rights options
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain the tradeoffs between 12-month owned-channel usage, paid social usage, and perpetual usage for this campaign: [campaign details].

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a negotiation brief
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a clause-by-clause negotiation brief for this proposed influencer deal. Include preferred positions, acceptable compromises, and issues requiring legal review: [paste deal terms].

output_examples.input: Draft an agreement for two Instagram posts for $500.
output: A scope section listing two Instagram posts and approval dates.
A payment section with the $500 fee and payment timing.
A 12-month non-exclusive owned-channel license and disclosure requirement.

output_examples.input: Review a contract with perpetual content rights.
output: Red flag: perpetual usage rights may exceed the agreed campaign value.
Negotiation option: limit rights to 12 or 24 months and define permitted channels.
Legal-review question: confirm whether paid advertising and sublicensing are included.

best_practices: Provide complete deal details before requesting a draft.
Define the scope, duration, channels, and compensation for every usage-rights grant.
Have qualified legal counsel review the final agreement before execution.
anti_patterns: Do not treat a generated template as jurisdiction-specific legal advice.
Do not leave deliverables, payment dates, or approval timelines undefined.
Do not grant perpetual or paid-media rights without clear scope and compensation.

faq.question: Is this skill a substitute for a lawyer?
faq.answer: No. It provides general guidance and templates. Have qualified legal counsel review any agreement before execution.

faq.question: Can it draft an agreement from a short brief?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide the parties, deliverables, compensation, platform, and requested rights. The skill can mark unknown terms as TBD.

faq.question: Can it review an agency contract?
faq.answer: Yes. Paste the relevant terms. It can identify missing terms and common negotiation concerns for legal review.

faq.question: Does it cover FTC disclosures?
faq.answer: Yes. The template includes sponsorship disclosure requirements, but you must confirm current legal and platform requirements.

faq.question: Can it negotiate with a creator?
faq.answer: It can prepare negotiation guidance. It does not conduct outreach or negotiate with external parties.

faq.question: What details are most important for usage rights?
faq.answer: Specify the channels, territory, duration, exclusivity, paid-media use, modifications, and compensation for the license.
